title: stability-staffflow-capacity-tuner-and-kpi-sandbox
summary: Working KPI sandbox that ties staff flow (oncall capacity and shift overlap) to infrastructure capacity tiers for staged launches. Purpose is to provide a small, executable decision surface for go/no-go gating that balances latency SLO, cost burn, and headcount availability. This is a working sheet used by Product Ops + Eng SRE during pilot/dedicated rollouts to tune staffing vs reserved GPU capacity and predefine fallback actions.
kpi_rows: KV cache hit ratio, >70%, 60-85%, <45% for 30m, eng-runtime, 30m
Avg queue wait time, <40ms, 0-60ms, >200ms for 5m, infra-ops, 5m
capacity_map:
Tiers
- Tier A (Green): Dedicated reserved pool (x8 A100), expected 500 rps, cold start 15s, use for full production flows.
- Tier B (Amber): Shared dedicated burst (mixed V100/A100), expected 150-300 rps, cold start 25s; used for canaries and staged expansion.
- Tier C (Red): Hosted fallback (smaller quantized variants), expected 50-120 rps, latency variance higher; used for emergency degradation.
Staffing mapping: Green => 2 oncall SRE + 1 product ops lead; Amber => 1 oncall SRE + rotating engineer; Red => minimal oncall + escalation to multi-team.
Cost knobs: autoscale cooldown 60s, max-burst policy enabled, prefix cache TTL 5m for surge traffic.
Notes: map is intentionally conservative for first 72h after traffic ramp; revisit after 7d telemetry window.
triggers_and_thresholds: If p95 latency >400ms sustained for 10 minutes: immediately shift 30% of traffic to Tier C quantized model and notify SRE pager (P1).
If error rate >1% for 5 minutes: pause incremental rollout and rollback last model variant; open incident and allocate 2-hr debug slot.
If cost per 1k tokens >$0.03 for 1 hour: enable cost-saver quantization on non-critical routes and reduce batch windows by 20%.
If queue wait time >200ms for 5 minutes: scale Tier B pool by 1 additional node and re-evaluate batching policy.
contingency_playbook: Runbook step 1: Triage on-call to confirm signal source (model, infra, network). Attach last 50 traces to incident ticket.
Runbook step 2: If infra-related, activate pre-warmed node from reserved pool; document node id and time to availability.
Runbook step 3: If model regression suspected, cut traffic to previous pinned model version and mark new variant as quarantined.
Runbook step 4: Communicate status to stakeholders via #launch-ops channel and update public status page if customer-visible impact.
Runbook step 5: After stabilization, run postmortem within 48 hours and update this sheet with corrective actions and metric deltas.
rollout_checklist: Config: pinned model version in platform and fallback variant validated (yes/no)
Observability: dashboards (latency, errors, cost) shared and permissioned to oncall group
Staffing: oncall roster confirmed for 72h with overlap windows annotated
Capacity: Tier A/B nodes pre-provisioned and smoke tested
Traffic plan: ramp schedule (0-10-25-50-100 percent) with dwell times and rollback windows
Communication: incident channel created and customer-facing status plan ready
Playbook: contingency steps reviewed with SRE and product ops (signed off)
open_risks: Quantized fallback may produce quality regressions on long-form prompts; need golden set evals pre-approved.
Staffing: two critical owners (eng + sre) on PTO during target launch weekend — backup must be confirmed.
Capacity provisioning in eu-west-1 constrained by cloud partner maintenance window (2026-02-28).
Cost: burst autoscaling may exceed cost guardrails if traffic pattern becomes spiky — need burst cap policy test.
